bodyBlocks.html: Most delays in business funding aren't about credit — they're about paperwork. Having your documents ready before you shop makes every conversation faster.

• Business tax returns — typically the last two years.
  • Personal financial statement — for owners with significant ownership.
  • Bank statements — often the most recent six months.
  • Debt schedule — a summary of existing business obligations.
  • Use-of-funds summary — what you'll do with the capital.
For acquisitions, add the target business's financials and a purchase agreement or letter of intent.

Traditionally, each lender wants its own copies in its own format. Prepare a clean set once and you remove one of the biggest sources of friction. Fund44 uses approved workflow wording about one document checklist and document reuse only where that support is available in the experience.

1. Gather the five documents above in PDF.
  2. Write a two-paragraph use-of-funds summary.
  3. Note your desired amount and rough timeline.
  4. Check your options and see which paths fit.

commonQuestions.question: Do I need a business plan?
commonQuestions.answer: For some loan types and acquisitions, a plan or use-of-funds narrative helps. For flexible working-capital products, recent financials often matter more.

commonQuestions.question: Does uploading documents to Fund44 trigger a credit check?
commonQuestions.answer: Checking the preview uses information that does not affect your credit score because the current preview does not submit an application to a lender.
